question: In which year was the Nobel prize awarded jointly to Eric A Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl E Wieman 'for the achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle, and Carl E. Wieman were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in **2001**.
 
• The award was given for their groundbreaking work on the **achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC)** in dilute gases of alkali atoms.
 
• This was the first experimental realization of Bose-Einstein condensation, a state of matter predicted by **Satyendra Nath Bose** and Albert Einstein in the 1920s.
 
• Their research opened up new possibilities for exploring quantum mechanics and studying matter under extreme conditions.
 
• The Nobel Committee recognized this achievement as a significant milestone in the field of atomic physics and quantum mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bose-Einstein Condensation (BEC):**

 
 
• BEC is a state of matter formed when a gas of bosons is cooled to temperatures very close to absolute zero (0 Kelvin).
 
• Under such extreme conditions, a large fraction of the atoms occupy the same quantum state, forming a "superatom" with unique quantum properties.
 
 
 
• **Satyendra Nath Bose's Contribution:**
 
 
• Indian physicist Satyendra Nath Bose worked on the statistical mechanics of particles that obey Bose-Einstein statistics, known as bosons.
 
• Albert Einstein extended Bose's work to predict the phenomenon of BEC in the 1920s.
 
 
 
• **Experimental Setup by Nobel Laureates:**
 
 
• Cornell and Wieman used a combination of laser cooling and evaporative cooling techniques to achieve BEC in rubidium atoms in 1995.
 
• Ketterle refined the technique and demonstrated new properties of BEC, such as interference patterns between condensates.
 
 
 
• **Applications of BEC:**
 
 
• Bose-Einstein condensates are used to study quantum phenomena such as superfluidity and quantum vortices.
 
• They have potential applications in precision measurement, quantum computing, and simulations of complex quantum systems.
